title: PR #36990 added the support app's CourseTeamManageAPIView with only IsAuthenticated, without the support-role gate every sibling support view uses, so any learner can probe arbitrary accounts and instructors can read other users' course roles.

findings.explanation: The diff does not introduce any SQL queries or raw SQL operations. All database queries use Django ORM methods (filter, exists) which provide parameterization by default. The email/username parameters come from query parameters but are only used with ORM methods, not raw SQL strings.

The authorization check added in the `get` method (line 247) gates access to course team information via `_caller_can_manage_course_team()`. However, the underlying `list()` method and the email/username query parameter handling still require verification that the requested user data being fetched belongs to or is authorized for the requesting user. The check ensures the caller has permission to reach the endpoint, but doesn't verify that fetching details about an arbitrary email address via the query parameter respects proper authorization boundaries. The test regression comments mention GHSA-95xv-3c54-c3pw which suggests this was an enumeration vulnerability where any authenticated user could query arbitrary emails. The new check returns 403 early for plain learners, but there's insufficient evidence in the diff that the underlying list logic prevents IDOR when a support staff or instructor queries arbitrary users they shouldn't have access to.

evidence.content:
def _caller_can_manage_course_team(self, auth_user):
        """
        Return True if the caller may view or manage course team roles.

        This is the union of the PUT authorization set (`is_staff`,
        `is_superuser`, or any user with a `CourseAccessRole` of
        `role="instructor"`) and the global `SupportStaffRole`. Read access
        must at least match write access — a user who can PUT changes needs
        to see the current state to make them — and the endpoint lives in
        the support module, so support staff belong in the set too.
        """
        if (
            auth_user.is_superuser
            or auth_user.is_staff
            or SupportStaffRole().has_user(auth_user)
        ):
            return True
        return CourseAccessRole.objects.filter(
            user=auth_user, role="instructor"
        ).exists()

findings.suggested_fix: Verify that the email/username query parameter being used in the list view corresponds to either the authenticated user themselves or a user they are authorized to inspect (e.g., based on course enrollment relationships or explicit delegation). The authorization check gates the endpoint but doesn't validate the scope of the data being queried within that endpoint.
